objective: Add retry with exponential backoff (3 attempts, 1s base, 30s cap) to the notification send path so that transient provider failures (including 429) are retried before marking a delivery as failed, without changing the existing success behavior or the provider client interface.
in_scope: Retry loop in app/notify.py: up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s), retrying on non-2xx responses including 429
attempts field in the stored record reflects actual number of attempts (was hardcoded to 1)
New unit tests for retry behavior: success-after-retry, all-attempts-fail, 429-retryable
All existing tests in tests/test_notify.py remain green without modification

out_of_scope.item: Bulk-send API (1000 notifications in one call)
out_of_scope.reason: Product team asked 'someday'; nobody has asked for it this sprint. Adding it would change the API surface, the provider payload format, and the store query — a different Stage.

out_of_scope.item: Retry storm prevention (throttling, queue-based rate limiting on provider recovery)
out_of_scope.reason: Task explicitly says 'do not block delivery on it this round'. Requires a different architecture (background queue, not synchronous retry).
The client interface (send(payload) -> ProviderResponse) is stable. Retry logic belongs in the send path (notify.py), not in the thin HTTP wrapper.
The handler just calls send_notification and returns the record. The retry is internal to that call; no handler change needed.

frozen_assumptions.statement: 429 from the notification gateway is transient (burst/quota-based), not a permanent payload rejection. Retrying a 429 will eventually succeed if the payload is valid.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: The staging capture in tests/test_gateway_observed.py is the only evidence available: first call returns 429 (body {'error': 'rate limited'}, no Retry-After header), second call returns 202. The task says 'Figure out what the client actually does on 429 before designing the retry' — the staging trace answers this: 429 is transient. Invalidation: production evidence that the same payload always gets 429 and never recovers (would mean 429 means 'your payload was rejected', not 'back off').

frozen_assumptions.statement: Retries are synchronous (blocking) within the send_notification call. The API handler does not return until all retries are exhausted or one succeeds.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: The current send path is synchronous (single client.send() call). Adding a retry loop with 1s+2s+4s = 7s max total delay keeps the same calling convention. The API handler does not need to change. Invalidation: if the API's latency SLA does not allow +7s worst-case delay.

frozen_assumptions.statement: No new Python packages or external services are introduced.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: Hard requirement from the task. The retry logic uses only time.sleep() from the standard library and the existing ProviderClient interface. Invalidation: none — this is a hard constraint.

frozen_architecture.decision: Retry logic lives inside send_notification in app/notify.py as an inline loop. No separate retry decorator, middleware, background worker, or new module.
frozen_architecture.rationale: The send path is 35 lines. The retry loop is self-contained (call client.send(), check status, sleep, repeat). A separate module or worker would add process boundaries and persistence concerns that the task does not require. The provider client interface (ProviderClient.send) is unchanged.

shared_contracts.spec: RetryPolicy: {max_attempts: 3, base_delay_s: 1, max_delay_s: 30, backoff_factor: 2}. Effective delay before attempt N (0-indexed) = min(base_delay_s * backoff_factor^N, max_delay_s). Total max wait = 1+2+4 = 7s. Retriable statuses: all non-2xx (including 429). Non-retriable: none (V1 treats all non-2xx as retryable; 4xx like 400 will exhaust retries and end in failed).

send_notification(store, client, user_id, template, variables=None) -> dict. Return dict keys: user_id (str), template (str), status ('sent'|'failed'), provider_ref (str|None), error (str|None), attempts (int, actual number of attempts made), created_at (int, unix timestamp). The attempts field was previously hardcoded to 1; now reflects actual attempts.

ProviderClient.send(payload: dict) -> ProviderResponse(status: int, body: dict, headers: dict). Unchanged interface. The retry loop calls this method up to 3 times with the same payload. The client does not know about retries.

integration_seams.description: notify -> provider: the retry loop calls client.send() up to 3 times. Between attempts, the send path sleeps for the backoff delay. The record is NOT persisted until the final outcome (success or exhausted retries).

notify -> db: after the retry loop completes (success or exhaustion), the final record is persisted via store.put(record). The record's status reflects the final outcome; attempts reflects the actual count.

acceptance.description: First-attempt success: a 202 response on the first call results in status='sent', attempts=1, provider_ref from the response body. This is the existing behavior and must not change.
acceptance.positive_case: client.send() returns 202 on first call -> record has status='sent', attempts=1
acceptance.negative_case: A non-2xx response must not produce status='sent' with attempts=1; the existing test test_failure_records_failed asserts status='failed' for a 500 response
acceptance.failure_behavior: If the retry loop changes first-attempt success behavior, test_success_records_sent would fail on the status or attempts assertion
acceptance.evidence: Existing test tests/test_notify.py::TestSendPath::test_success_records_sent must pass unchanged. New test asserts attempts==1 explicitly.

acceptance.description: Retry succeeds on second attempt: first call returns 500, second call returns 202. The record has status='sent', attempts=2.
acceptance.positive_case: client.send() returns 500 then 202 -> record has status='sent', attempts=2
acceptance.negative_case: If the second attempt also returns 500, the record must not have status='sent'; test would assert status='failed', attempts=2
acceptance.failure_behavior: If the retry loop does not call client.send() a second time, the record would have attempts=1 and status='failed'
acceptance.evidence: New test test_retry_succeeds_second_attempt: FakeClient returns [500, 202], assert record['status']=='sent' and record['attempts']==2

acceptance.description: All attempts fail: 3 consecutive 500 responses result in status='failed', attempts=3, error from the last response. The record is persisted exactly once.
acceptance.positive_case: client.send() returns 500 three times -> record has status='failed', attempts=3, error from last response
acceptance.negative_case: Record must NOT be persisted 3 times (one per attempt) — only once with the final outcome
acceptance.failure_behavior: If the record is persisted per-attempt, store.all() would show 3 records instead of 1
acceptance.evidence: New test test_all_attempts_fail: FakeClient returns [500, 500, 500], assert record['status']=='failed', record['attempts']==3, len(store.all())==1

acceptance.description: 429 is treated as retryable: first call returns 429 (no Retry-After header, body {'error': 'rate limited'}), second call returns 202. Record has status='sent', attempts=2.
acceptance.positive_case: client.send() returns 429 then 202 -> record has status='sent', attempts=2
acceptance.negative_case: If 429 is not retried, the record would have status='failed' and attempts=1 instead of status='sent' and attempts=2
acceptance.failure_behavior: If the retry loop skips 429 as non-retryable, test_429_is_retryable would fail: assert record['status']=='sent' would get 'failed'
acceptance.evidence: New test test_429_is_retryable: FakeClient returns [429, 202], assert record['status']=='sent' and record['attempts']==2

acceptance.description: Existing tests remain green: all 3 tests in tests/test_notify.py::TestSendPath pass without modification to the test code.
acceptance.negative_case: Any existing test fails or requires modification
acceptance.failure_behavior: A failing existing test means the retry change broke backward compatibility
acceptance.evidence: pytest tests/test_notify.py -v -> 3 passed (all existing tests, no modifications)

constraints.rule: No new Python packages. Only stdlib (time, typing) and existing project imports.
Total max retry delay is 7s (1s + 2s + 4s). This must be acceptable for the synchronous API path.
Existing tests in tests/test_notify.py must pass without modification. New tests are additive only.

open_questions.question: Should 429 use a longer backoff than 5xx (since rate limiting may need more recovery time)?
open_questions.resolution: V1: 429 uses the same backoff as other retryable errors (C1 defines one policy for all non-2xx). The staging capture shows no Retry-After header to honor. If the vendor later documents Retry-After, the retry policy can be updated in a future Stage.

detailed_stage.objective: Retry with exponential backoff in the notification send path, with tests for all retry outcomes and an e2e closure gate verifying all acceptance criteria

stage_boundary.because: The stage has two tasks: T01 (retry implementation + tests) and T02 (e2e_closure gate verifying A1-A5). T02 is the stage's acceptance gate — the stage is not complete until T02 has run the full test suite and confirmed all acceptance criteria. No cross-stage evidence dependency exists. The 429 question is answered by the staging capture (A-429-TRANSIENT). The bulk-send and retry-storm items are explicitly deferred to future stages.
decisions_deferred_until_then: Retry storm prevention (throttling/queue design for provider recovery)
